questions.problem:
A rumor is spreading in a city. The rate of growth in the number of people $P(t)$ who heard the rumor follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=12P-0.000\,2{P}^{2},\,P(0)=2\,000.
$$

where $t$ is the time, measured in hours. For which value of $P$ is the number of people who heard the rumor growing at the fastest possible rate?
questions.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
{P}^{′}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

For a logistic growth model, the fastest rate of growth occurs when $P=\frac{1}{2}a.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200098/assets/9d8f5340bba4d3c407e43f2bc64a4aa2ea986be89b8024baaa4e8ae65e96e5d5.png)

First, let's rewrite the right-hand side of the given equation so that it matches the form above:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{dt} & =12P-0.000\,2{P}^{2} \\  & =0.000\,02P(60\,000-P)\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that $a=60\,000.$ Hence, the carrying capacity is $60\,000,$ and $P$ grows at its fastest possible rate when 

$$
P=\frac{1}{2}a=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 60\,000=30\,000.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following differential equation for the function $y=y(t):$

$$
{y}^{′}=1\,000y-10{y}^{2},\,y(0)=40
$$

What is ${lim}_{t\to \infty }y(t)?$
questions.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
{y}^{′}=ky(a-y),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>y$ is the carrying capacity.

A diagram showing a typical logistic growth curve is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200098/assets/57f4b604c546daed4f1cb3895191fae0ccac33b5c17aac705f203f0a837c7e69.png)

First, let's factor the right-hand side of the given equation. This gives

$$
{y}^{′}=10y(100-y),\,y(0)=40.
$$

From here, we see that $a=100.$ Hence, the carrying capacity is $100.$

For a given logistic growth model, $y\to a$ as $t\to \infty .$ Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{t\to \infty }y(t)=100.
$$

questions.problem:
The population $y(t)$ of beavers in a river follows the logistic growth model

$$
{y}^{′}=0.2y(8-\frac{y}{100}),\,y(0)=200,
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years, since the observations began. According to this model, what is the maximum possible beaver population?
questions.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
{y}^{′}=ky(a-y),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>y$ is the carrying capacity. 

The carrying capacity $a$ represents the maximum possible population. A diagram showing a typical logistic growth curve is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200098/assets/57f4b604c546daed4f1cb3895191fae0ccac33b5c17aac705f203f0a837c7e69.png)

First, let's rewrite the right-hand side of the given equation so that it matches the form above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =0.2y(8-\frac{y}{100}) \\  & =0.2y(\frac{800-y}{100}) \\  & =\frac{0.2y}{100}(800-y) \\  & =0.002y(800-y)\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that $a=800.$ Hence, the carrying capacity is $800,$ and we conclude that the number of beavers cannot exceed $800.$

$$

where $t$ is the time, in years, since the observations began. According to this model, what is the maximum possible population of elephants?
questions.worked_solution:

$$

$$
